summary: Analysis of 14 days of CGM and AAPS telemetry (3,995 valid CGM readings, 98.7% coverage) reveals strong overall baseline control with an average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL and 86.0% Time in Range. However, significant safety risks are present: total Time Below Range is 5.1% (exceeding the clinical target of <4.0%), driven by frequent overnight hypoglycemia (up to 18.5% TBR at 01:00 local) and late-afternoon reactive dips (15.3% TBR at 19:00 local). Because 0 grams of meal carbohydrates were logged during the period, the system relies entirely on Unannounced Meal (UAM) processing and auto-SMBs. Aggressive Dynamic ISF scaling combined with high Max IOB safety ceilings (25 U) and GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying leads to late insulin stacking after postprandial surges.

analysis_steps.findings: High-density CGM telemetry with 98.7% coverage across 14 days. Active profile settings are complete. Zero meal carbohydrates were logged, indicating reliance on UAM automation.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 entries out of 4,046 expected; 10 gaps, largest gap 65.0 minutes; 0 g total carbs logged across 655 insulin treatments.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of logged meal carbs and timestamps prevents direct mathematical validation of Carb Ratios.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall control is strong (86.0% TIR), but hypoglycemia risk is elevated (5.1% TBR), concentrating overnight (23:00-04:00 local) and early evening (18:00-19:00 local).
analysis_steps.evidence: Mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, CV 32.6%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%. Sensor lows reached 41-42 mg/dL on multiple days. TBR peaks at 18.5% at 01:00 local and 15.3% at 19:00 local.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of carbohydrate treatment entries obscures whether low readings resolved spontaneously or required fast-acting carbs.

analysis_steps.findings: Fasting morning basal (05:00-09:00) is accurate and holds glucose stable at ~100 mg/dL. Overnight target (90 mg/dL) combined with lingering post-dinner IOB increases nocturnal hypo risk.
analysis_steps.evidence: 05:00-08:00 mean glucose 99.5-104.2 mg/dL with 95.2%-98.7% TIR and <4.8% TBR. 00:00-03:00 local TBR ranges from 10.1% to 18.5% under a 90 mg/dL target.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Unlogged bedtime snacks or variable sleep times cannot be isolated without event notes.

analysis_steps.findings: DIA of 10.0 hours is appropriate. Baseline ISF of 56 mg/dL/U is scaled dynamically down to <30 mg/dL/U during postprandial surges, causing post-peak over-delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: Profile DIA = 10.0 h. Loop logs show dynamic ISF scaling down to 27.8-37.9 mg/dL/U during highs above 240 mg/dL, driving subsequent drops of >160 mg/dL over 2-4 hours.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of manual bolus entries prevents decoupling baseline CR from dynamic ISF adjustments.

analysis_steps.findings: With zero logged carbs, UAM and SMBs handle 100% of meal insulin delivery. High Max UAM SMB Basal Minutes (20 min) front-loads excessive insulin into slow GLP-1 absorption curves.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min. IOB reaches up to 5.9 U following afternoon unannounced meals.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact meal start times are unrecorded, obscuring the lag between carb ingestion and UAM detection.

analysis_steps.findings: Max IOB (25 U) exceeds Total Daily Dose (~19.7 U/day), and Max Basal (12 U/h) is 15x peak profile basal, creating severe safety risks during unannounced meal stacking.
analysis_steps.evidence: Profile max_iob_units=25.0 U vs average TDD of 19.7 U/day; max_basal_u_per_hour=12.0 U/h vs peak profile basal of 0.8 U/h.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Sensor noise or compression artifact instances cannot be fully separated without user annotations.

analysis_steps.findings: Relying strictly on UAM creates a timing mismatch: insulin peaks after glucose has already peaked, while concurrent GLP-1 therapy delays gastric emptying.
analysis_steps.evidence: Mean afternoon glucose peaks at 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00 local (TAR 32.1%), followed by a sharp drop to 105.4 mg/dL at 19:00 local (TBR 15.3%). GLP-1 1.25 mg notes logged on Aug 14, 17, 20.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of meal carb entries prevents evaluating prebolus timing or standard bolus distribution.

analysis_steps.findings: Extended glucose elevations lasting 4-6 hours post-meal reflect GLP-1 delayed gastric emptying, which standard UAM algorithms misinterpret as persistent rapid spikes.
analysis_steps.evidence: Postprandial response curves show lingering highs lasting 3-5 hours, followed by steep late falls as SMB insulin outlives carb absorption.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero e-carb entries exist in telemetry; absorption patterns are inferred from CGM curves and GLP-1 notes.

analysis_steps.findings: Synthesized findings prioritize capping safety parameters first, adjusting the overnight target to mitigate nocturnal lows second, and introducing meal logging with e-carbs third.
analysis_steps.evidence: High Max IOB (25 U) combined with nocturnal TBR (18.5%) and UAM postprandial swings supports a conservative 3-step safety plan.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Validation requires sequential execution and 3-5 days of observation between changes.

strengths: Excellent CGM data coverage (98.7%) over the 14-day evaluation window.
Outstanding daytime Time in Range (86.0% overall), with highly stable fasting control between 05:00 and 09:00 local time.
Appropriately set DIA (10.0 hours) preventing premature insulin-on-board accounting decay.
issues: Elevated overall hypoglycemia (5.1% TBR), concentrating overnight (up to 18.5% TBR at 01:00 local) and early evening (15.3% TBR at 19:00 local).
Excessively high safety limits: Max IOB is set to 25 U (exceeding TDD of 19.7 U/day) and Max Basal is set to 12 U/h (15x peak basal).
Complete absence of meal carb logging, forcing total reliance on UAM automation that stacks insulin during GLP-1 delayed carb absorption curves.

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Target to Reduce Nocturnal Lows
recommendations.description: Increase the target glucose from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00 to reduce nocturnal time below range (currently up to 18.5%).

recommendations.title: Reduce Max IOB and Max Basal Safety Ceilings
recommendations.description: Lower Max IOB from 25 U to 8.0 U (approx. 40% of TDD) and Max Basal from 12 U/h to 3.2 U/h (4x peak profile basal) to prevent dangerous over-dosing during unannounced meal surges.

recommendations.title: Moderate Max UAM SMB Basal Minutes
recommendations.description: Reduce Max UAM SMB Basal Minutes from 20 min to 15 min to curtail aggressive automated insulin delivery during unannounced meal spikes.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise target glucose segments from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight Time Below Range reaches up to 18.5% at 01:00 local time. Fasting morning basal (05:00-09:00) holds glucose steady around 100 mg/dL, indicating that the 90 mg/dL night target drives unnecessary low-temp suspensions and mild hypoglycemia.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe overnight sensor glucose for 3-5 nights to verify TBR drops below 4.0% without impacting waking glucose.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Log meal carbohydrates explicitly with a 10-15 minute prebolus. Deliver 50-60% of the calculated meal dose immediately and enter the remaining carbs as extended carbs (e-carbs over 2-3 hours) to match GLP-1 delayed gastric absorption and allow UAM/SMBs to act only as a backstop.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: GLP-1 therapy slows gastric emptying. Relying on UAM causes late insulin delivery that hits after carb absorption slows down, driving postprandial spikes followed by steep drops (15.3% TBR at 19:00 local). Front-loading half the dose and extending the rest prevents both early spikes and late rebound lows.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log meal carb amounts and timestamps for 3 consecutive days to observe postprandial glucose curves and assess CR accuracy.

exceptions.suggestion: Deliver 30% immediate bolus and extend 70% as e-carbs over 3-4 hours.
exceptions.rationale: Combined fat/protein and GLP-1 therapy prolongs carb absorption into the night; spreading insulin prevents 01:00-03:00 nocturnal lows.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Update safety ceiling limits in AAPS settings (Max IOB = 8.0 U, Max Basal = 3.2 U/h).
Step 2: Update the overnight target glucose in the profile from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00.
Step 3: Monitor glucose overnight for 3-5 days to confirm nocturnal Time Below Range drops below 4.0%.
Step 4: Reduce Max UAM SMB Basal Minutes from 20 min to 15 min in AAPS settings.
Step 5: Begin logging meal carbohydrates and testing a 50% upfront / 50% e-carb strategy for main meals.
education: GLP-1 receptor agonists significantly delay stomach emptying, which changes how quickly carbohydrates enter the bloodstream.
When meals are unannounced, closed-loop systems increase insulin delivery after glucose is already rising rapidly, which can lead to delayed insulin stacking once carb absorption slows down.
Setting Max IOB to a realistic ceiling (e.g., 40-50% of Total Daily Dose) acts as a crucial guardrail against automated over-dosing during prolonged high glucose readings.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only. Independently verify all proposed profile and automation changes before applying them.
Make parameter changes one at a time, allowing 3-5 days of observation between modifications.
Monitor sensor glucose closely during sleep and maintain fast-acting carbohydrates nearby for hypoglycemia treatment.
